summary:
This project explores the fundamental principles of telescopes, major astronomical observation projects, and the search for Planet X. The light-gathering capacity and angular resolution of telescopes play a crucial role in observing distant celestial objects. Techniques such as photometry, spectroscopy, and astrometry enable scientists to analyse the brightness, chemical composition, and movements of stars.

The S-PLUS project aims to create a three-dimensional map of the universe by using the T80-South telescope in Chile and twelve different optical filters. Artificial intelligence is also employed to analyse millions of galaxies and quasars. Furthermore, the spectrum of Sirius A is studied to gain valuable insights into stellar atmospheres and chemical properties.

Another major topic discussed in the PDF is Planet X. This hypothetical planet, believed to potentially exist beyond Neptune, has not yet been directly observed. Its possible existence is suggested by the unusual orbital patterns of certain small celestial objects. Advanced telescopic observations aim to contribute to the eventual discovery of Planet X.
details: This project focuses on studying the structure of the universe, stars, and galaxies using advanced telescope systems such as SPHEREx and S-PLUS. By analyzing different wavelengths of light, scientists investigate the distances, chemical compositions, and properties of celestial objects. It also explores the possibility of detecting Planet X, a hypothetical planet believed to exist in the distant regions of our Solar System. The main goal is to explain how modern astronomical technologies help us understand the universe and discover new celestial objects.
